lead.headline: Quiet Columbus Day open: Salesforce jumps, Adobe slides, Brent holds near $106
lead.dek: Index levels are early-session estimates (10:23 a.m. ET, 17:23 Kuwait). Stocks trade normally today, but the US cash bond market is closed and no data is due.
body: US stocks opened little changed. By 10:23 a.m. ET the S&P 500 was up 0.05%, the Dow up 0.19% and the Nasdaq down 0.07%, with small caps (+0.46%) doing best. Single-stock analyst calls are doing the work: Salesforce rose 4.3% after BofA's double upgrade, while Adobe fell 4% after Wells Fargo's double downgrade.

Oil swung both ways. Brent dipped toward $103 in Asia on Trump's Russian diesel deal and his claimed Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire', then recovered to about $106 (+1.2%) after Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport and tanker attacks near Oman and Hormuz. Iran called the US response to its peace terms 'inadequate'.
Watch for Tuesday's bank results (JPM, GS, C, WFC) and Wednesday's September CPI. The 10-year yield sits at 5.24% from Friday's close.

side.headline: Bank earnings start Tuesday as the market looks for its next driver
side.summary: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citi and Wells Fargo report before Tuesday's open, with Bank of America and Morgan Stanley on Wednesday. Consensus EPS: JPM $5.93, GS $13.04, C $2.65, WFC $1.85. Investors want to see whether trading revenue offsets the funding pressure from a 5%+ 10-year yield.

side.headline: Busy data week: CPI Wednesday, then PPI and retail sales Thursday
side.summary: Tuesday brings NFIB small-business optimism and existing home sales. Wednesday has September CPI and the Beige Book, and Thursday has PPI, retail sales, Empire State, Philly Fed and jobless claims. The 2-year yield closed Friday at 4.79%.

side.headline: Markets price about a 19% chance of another Fed hike this month
side.summary: CME FedWatch shows an 18.8% probability of a hike at the Oct 27-28 FOMC. Cleveland Fed's Hammack and Chair Warsh speak Thursday (US time). Trump also said the US may join Saudi Arabia in strikes on the Houthis.

events.text: Columbus Day: NYSE/Nasdaq open, US cash bond market closed, no US economic data
IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok (through Oct 18); Aptos (APT) unlocks about 11.31M tokens
NFIB small business optimism; bank earnings pre-market (JPM, GS, C, WFC)
US September CPI and core CPI; Beige Book at 21:00
PPI, retail sales, Empire State, Philly Fed, jobless claims; Hammack 23:30, Warsh Fri 06:30

picks.name: Salesforce
picks.catalyst: BofA double-upgraded the stock to Buy from Underperform and raised its target to $285 from $160. The gap held into the open, with shares up 4.3% at 10:23 a.m. ET.
picks.bull: A sell-side reversal this sharp, plus a gap that held after the open, is a setup for follow-through. Watch for the stock to hold above Friday's close through the session.
picks.bear: Software is under pressure with 5%+ yields. Wells Fargo cut Adobe the same day, so the sector call isn't unanimous, and gap-fades are common before CPI.

picks.name: Biogen
picks.catalyst: JPMorgan upgraded it to Overweight and raised its target to $300 from $210, citing pipeline catalysts expected by 2027 beyond Leqembi. Shares rose about 2.1% premarket.
picks.bull: Defensive healthcare with a fresh re-rating argument. It offers some cover if CPI or yields knock growth stocks.
picks.bear: The catalysts run to 2027, so this is slow money. Clinical readouts are binary, and the MS franchise keeps eroding.
picks.invalidation: Close below Friday's pre-upgrade close would negate the catalyst

picks.name: Microsoft
picks.catalyst: It unveiled the Maia 300, its third-generation custom AI chip, and plans to deploy potentially more than 1 million units next year. Shares were up 0.7% early.
picks.bull: In-house silicon could lower AI infrastructure costs and reduce reliance on Nvidia. A likely setup if the market rotates back into megacap quality.
picks.bear: Chip benefits take years to show in margins. High yields cap tech valuations, and the move so far is small.
picks.invalidation: Close below Friday's close would show the news isn't being rewarded

picks.name: AST SpaceMobile
picks.catalyst: BlueBird 14-16 satellites arrived at Cape Canaveral ahead of launch, and the FCC cleared 900-MHz testing. Shares rose 3.9% early.
picks.bull: Launch and regulatory milestones are concrete, and SpaceX's $8B spectrum deal has put direct-to-device stocks in focus.
picks.bear: HIGH RISK: a very volatile, pre-profit name. SpaceX's Starlink Mobile push is also a direct competitive threat, and launch delays are common.

picks.name: Bitcoin
picks.catalyst: It is testing $84,000 resistance after $681M of weekly spot ETF outflows, the most since June. Analysts flag $82,000 as the support bulls need to hold before Wednesday's CPI.
picks.bull: Short unwinds pushed it above $84K earlier today, and nine of the top ten coins rose. A daily close above $84K would be the setup to watch.
picks.bear: ETF selling plus 24-year-high yields are a strong headwind. A hot CPI could push it back toward the 50-day EMA.

news.headline: Microsoft unveils Maia 300 AI chip; IonQ buys Elisity
news.summary: Microsoft rose 0.7% on its third-generation custom AI chip. IonQ fell 3.1% after agreeing to buy cybersecurity firm Elisity for up to $1.3 billion in stock.

news.headline: CCC jumps 10% on report GTCR and Elliott near a takeover
news.summary: Bloomberg reported that private equity firm GTCR and activist Elliott are in advanced talks to acquire the auto insurance software provider. No deal has been announced.

news.headline: Brent recovers to $106 after dipping on the Russian diesel deal
news.summary: Crude fell in Asia on Trump's deal for 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel and his claimed energy truce. It then rebounded on Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport and tanker attacks near Oman and Hormuz. Ukraine said it hadn't been consulted.

news.headline: Starbucks denies Chipotle bid; CMG falls, SBUX rises
news.summary: Starbucks denied a report that it was exploring a Chipotle acquisition. Chipotle fell 2.8% and Starbucks rose 1.3%. Delta slipped 0.9% after delaying its Atlanta-Riyadh route to March.

news.headline: Upgrades: CRM, BIIB, FSLR, TMUS. Downgrades: ADBE, HUBS, GDDY, PLTR
news.summary: Wells Fargo cut Adobe to Underweight (target $225 from $270), and Barclays cut HubSpot. JPMorgan upgraded Biogen to Overweight, and Evercore started Robinhood at Outperform.

news.headline: Bitcoin pulls back from $84K as ETFs bleed $681M on the week
news.summary: Spot bitcoin ETFs had their largest weekly outflow since June, and ether ETFs lost $542M. XRP ETFs took in $11M. Altcoins like AVAX and NEAR gained 8-12%.

avoid.reason: Wells Fargo double-downgraded it to Underweight (target $225, from $270), and it was down 4% early. It's a negative catalyst in software while yields stay above 5%.
Down 4.3% on weak lithium pricing, lower earnings estimates and cautious analyst views. No turn in the fundamentals yet.
J-Star is up about 153% premarket on a drone-frame expansion announcement. HIGH RISK: a micro-cap, low-liquidity spike that is prone to sharp reversals.

shifts: This edition was written about an hour after the US open; the earlier edition (No. 2) used premarket data. Indexes are still flat, as futures suggested.
CRM: the gap held, with shares up 4.3% and well above the $229.13 invalidation, so it stays on the list. BIIB: the upgrade move (+2.1% premarket) is intact, so it stays.
FSLR was dropped. No fresh data on today's move after the Truist upgrade could be verified, so the setup can't be confirmed. No previous pick hit its invalidation level.

New picks: MSFT (Maia 300 chip), ASTS (launch/FCC milestones, high risk) and BTC (an $84K resistance test). ADBE stays on the avoid list and fell further (-2.6% to -4%). ALB was added; IREN and MNDR were dropped for lack of fresh data.
Oil was volatile: Brent dipped toward $103 in Asia, then returned to about $106. Crypto is mixed, with BTC slightly lower and ETH up about 1%.

crypto.note: It briefly topped $84K before pulling back. Spot ETFs lost $681M last week, the most since June. Support is at $82K and the 50-day EMA (~$80.2K); resistance is at $84K, then $88K.
ETH ETFs had $542M of weekly outflows. It is holding the 50-day EMA (~$2,506); resistance is at the $2,600 supply zone.
It was the weakest of the four over the week. The 7-day change is from Oct 11 data, and the Alpenglow mainnet is expected this month.
XRP ETFs took in $11M last week, one of few inflows. It is testing the 50-day EMA (~$1.40); the 200-day EMA (~$1.38) is the next support.
